text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a classic public goods game where each contributed token returns 3x total value split evenly among 4 members, making full contribution socially optimal even though free-riding is individually dominant. I'm weighing whether to cooperate fully to maximize group welfare or protect against exploitation, given this plays out over 10 repeated rounds.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game: each token I contribute returns only 0.75 to me but 3 to the group, so individually defecting is the dominant strategy even though full cooperation maximizes everyone's payoff at 15 vs 20 each when all keep.

Since this is repeated over 10 rounds, cooperation might still be worthwhile. I'll contribute 10 as a moderate opening move to signal willingness to cooperate, then adapt based on others' behavior in later rounds.
